notes: the happy path: a whole-string decimal integer parses
the totality rule (ADR-0011): a conversion that cannot produce a value of the target type pushes :undefined, never an error

the propagation rule (ADR-0011): :undefined::type is :undefined for every target. user.missing is a genuine :undefined from an access miss, not a load of an absent root, which errors under the default on_unbound policy (see errors.json) and is a separate concern from cast's own semantics
float::integer truncates toward zero, deliberately diverging from PostgreSQL's rounding, to match Elixir trunc/JavaScript Math.trunc/Ruby to_i - -1.5 truncates to -1, not -2
chained-cast composition (ADR-0011): date::datetime is midnight UTC, and this is the supported spelling of a date-shaped string cast to datetime
the ISA has no truthiness rule and casts do not open a side door between booleans and numbers
identity clause: an integer already of the target type passes through unchanged
identity clause: a float already of the target type passes through unchanged
identity clause: a string already of the target type passes through unchanged
identity clause: a boolean already of the target type passes through unchanged
identity clause: a date already of the target type passes through unchanged
identity clause: a datetime already of the target type passes through unchanged
identity clause: a duration already of the target type passes through unchanged
integer::float widens exactly (below 2^53, where every integer has an exact float representation)
float::integer truncates toward zero at positive values too - 1.9 truncates to 1, not rounds to 2
integer::string is decimal formatting

float::string is normative only on the subset where exponent notation never kicks in and no trailing .0 ambiguity arises (px-2r5.3 notes); 3.5 formats identically across Elixir, JS, and Ruby's shortest-round-trip printers
the integer string-parse grammar accepts an optional leading minus
the float string-parse grammar accepts a bare integer form - "3"::float is 3.0, not :undefined
the float string-parse grammar accepts an optional leading minus with a fractional part
boolean string-parse accepts exactly the lowercase literal "true"
boolean string-parse accepts exactly the lowercase literal "false"
date string-parse is ISO 8601 calendar date

datetime string-parse requires a UTC offset and succeeds here - chained on to ::date rather than asserted as a datetime value, deliberately: this case's subject is the offset requirement, and the fractional-seconds field of the parsed datetime, though normative now (docs/isa.md section 5, pinned by px-7t8's two casts/datetime::string-format cases above), is not what this case is testing. Chaining to ::date confirms the parse succeeded and the calendar date is right without also asserting a fact this case doesn't own
duration string-parse is the language's own duration-literal grammar
boolean::string formats as the literal "true"
boolean::string formats as the literal "false"
date::string is ISO 8601 calendar date formatting
duration::string is the duration-literal grammar, largest unit first

datetime::string omits the fractional-seconds field entirely when the sub-second component is zero (docs/isa.md section 5, pinned by px-7t8). The sentence 'ISO 8601; datetimes in UTC with Z' did not determine this field, and the three implementations' host defaults disagreed on it - Elixir six digits, JavaScript three, Ruby none - so all three could claim ISA v4 while producing different strings for this cast. This case is the form, not one language's default

a non-zero sub-second component formats as exactly six digits, never a variable or minimal count (docs/isa.md section 5, px-7t8). The pinned value is expressible in milliseconds deliberately, so a JavaScript sibling backed by Date rather than Temporal can construct the input at all - the same portability discipline the float::string case applies. Note this also shows that datetime::string is a canonicalization and not a string identity: three input digits come back as six
the date::datetime bridge applied directly to a date literal, not by way of a string parse - midnight UTC, the same coercion compare and subtract already apply to a mixed pair
the datetime::date bridge takes the datetime's calendar date, discarding the time of day
the reverse direction of the seeded no-boolean-number-bridge case: the refusal is symmetric, not one-directional
a date has no numeric representation in the cast matrix - the catch-all rule, not a parse failure
an integer cannot become a date - only a string can, via ISO 8601 parsing
a duration has no numeric representation in the cast matrix
lists are not a cast source for any target - the catch-all rule covers structural values, not just scalar mismatches
maps are not a cast source for any target, including ::string - serialization is JSON.stringify's job, not a cast's
no partial consumption: the whole string must match, not a leading prefix of it
no trimming: leading (or trailing) whitespace makes the string unconvertible

regression for the anchoring defect fixed on px-2r5.3 (commit a06ba16): PCRE $ matches before a trailing newline, so an unanchored regex would have accepted "42\n" and then raised out of the string-to-integer parse. \A/\z anchors make this :undefined, per the totality rule, instead of an error
the totality rule applied to the float parse target
the float string-parse grammar has no exponent form, matching the language's own float literal grammar - "1e10" is not a whole-string decimal number
regression for the same anchoring defect fixed on px-2r5.3 (commit a06ba16), on the float parse path
boolean string-parse is case-sensitive: only the exact lowercase literals "true"/"false" match
the totality rule applied to the boolean parse target - no other truthy/falsy spellings are accepted
the totality rule applied to the date parse target
a syntactically ISO-8601-shaped string that names no real calendar date is still :undefined, not an error
a date-only string is :undefined for ::datetime - it has no UTC offset to parse. The supported spelling for this conversion is the chained ::date::datetime bridge, not a direct parse
the totality rule applied to the datetime parse target
the totality rule applied to the duration parse target
regression for the same anchoring defect fixed on px-2r5.3 (commit a06ba16): a trailing newline silently parsed as a valid duration before the fix, on top of the integer and float paths
the propagation rule holds for every target, not just ::integer - restated here for ::string
the propagation rule holds for every target, not just ::integer - restated here for ::date
propagation composes: :undefined::integer is :undefined, and :undefined::string is :undefined again - a chain of casts never recovers from an :undefined partway through
